questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: UBC has a very good geography programme + Canada has some beautiful nature. Furthermore, I wanted to experience the "campus-life" at a big university in North America, and I wanted to improve my English.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UBC was a good university, and I had many great experiences (academic and in my free time). But it was also challenging to study in a different way than in Denmark. University in Canada includes more mandatory elements than in Denmark.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Before arrival I got e-mails from UBC regarding moving in and starting at the university. Then we had a "welcome day" and we got a tour around campus + additional information about studying in Canada.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Good level of information. Once in Canada, I could go to the GoGlobal office if I needed any help, and they were very nice.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorms and shared units.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
If you lived in a dorm you had a meal plan, otherwise you had to cook your self. 
In my unit we had a oven and a standard size stovetop.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You have to buy kitchen appliances, cutlery, plates etc. yourself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in a nice apartment - two bathrooms for four people.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got an email every time I had a deadline.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I registered through the University of Copenhagen, and then again through UBC.
The application process has several rounds. First you just register, and then you have to choose courses later. You submit a list of 10 courses you want, and then get assigned four. It is possible to drop out/change courses the first two weeks of classes, so you can try a class and see if it is something for you if you are unsure.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mailing with GoGlobal before arriving. After arrival it was also very easy to just go to their office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't got the classes I wanted the most, but I was able to switch during the two first weeks of class. But I got assigned to courses on my list of 10 possible courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try different classes during the first two weeks, and don't be afraid to change class. It's very nice that you can try a class and just drop it again if you don't like it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very nice professors that cared about my learning.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took one first-year course, two second-year courses and a fourth-year course. 
The fourth-year course wasn't as difficult as I expected, and one of the second-year course was way more difficult than expected. So just read the course description to find out if it is too hard, and don't bother too much about the level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Very different.
The final grade is made up of one or more midterms, participation marks, small quizzes and a final. It was more like danish high school style.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EOSC 114: The catastrophic earth - Natural disasters. 
ATSC 201: Meteorology of storms.
NRES: 241: Introduction to Geomatics for Natural Resource Management
GEOG 497: The Arctic.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
NRES: 241: Introduction to Geomatics for Natural Resource Management. There is no final + it is nice to do computer lab. 
GEOG 497: The Arctic. Interesting and good course. Very nice professor.
EOSC 114: The catastrophic earth - Natural disasters. Quite easy first-year course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Expenses for apartment stuff when we moved in.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food is expensive (during groceries in the supermarket).
To go coffee and food is cheaper or same level as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is A LOT of clubs on campus that you can participate in.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of sports, crafting clubs, hiking clubs, book clubs, religious fellowships.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The Outdoor Club hosts a lot of nice hikes/trips.
I would recommend Rock Party with the outdoor club, which is a climbing trip to Squamish were you can learn to climb.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
See Vancouver, Stanley Park, Gastown.
Take a trip to Whistler and Bowen Island.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club on campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Canadians are very kind and nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. School can seem very overwhelming, but you will do fine even if you skip some classes.
2. Be prepared for public transportation in Vancouver. It is not as efficient as in Denmark. 
3. Don't be afraid to talk to the professors.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Save up money before you go. Canada is expensive.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying to live in another country and meet local people. I also really enjoyed the beautiful view to the mountains.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not feeling stressed about all the things I would like to experience. I had a bucket list of things I would like to see, but it was also overwhelming just to get my everyday life going.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Don't stress about all the things you would like to see and do, it is also okay to do nothing in your weekends.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
